newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban general jailed for drug trafficking freed.
newsitem.headline: Cuban general jailed for drug trafficking freed.

text.p: Cuban authorities have freed Patricio de la Guardia, a general condemned to 30 years in jail in 1989 during the "Ochoa" drug trafficking case, family sources said on Tuesday.
They said de la Guardia was freed late on Monday following the death of his father Mario de la Guardia, 96, and attended the funeral at Havana's Colon cemetery on Tuesday morning.
The sources told reporters they did not know if any conditions were attached to de la Guardia's early release, and it had come as a surprise.

De la Guardia, 58, declined to speak to reporters at the cemetery. Dressed in a short-sleeved patterned shirt, dark jeans and wearing sunglasses, he appeared thin but otherwise well. He has suffered in the past from stomach problems.
A former Interior Ministry general, he was convicted of drug trafficking and related offences at a trial of security forces officials that shocked the communist-ruled island.

His twin brother Antonio de la Guardia, an Interior Ministry colonel, was sentenced to death and executed in July 1989, along with a senior army general, Arnaldo Ochoa, and two other officers of the security forces.
Ochoa had headed Cuban forces fighting in Angola's civil war and was a decorated military hero before his disgrace.
Patricio de la Guardia was among 10 other officers given sentences ranging from 10 to 30 years in jail in the case.
There was no immediate comment on his release by the government of President Fidel Castro and no indication why he had been freed early.
